run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T14:47:31Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend-proxy RequestErrorRate alert is explained by a short, concentrated burst of failed checkout requests caused by the restart of the payment Deployment. At 2026-11-16T14:47:44Z the payment Deployment (otel-demo) rolled out a new ReplicaSet payment-79d86bf97f purely because a kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation was added (identical image, env and resources), the old pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 was killed at 14:47:49Z, and the replacement container (started 14:47:48Z) did not serve traffic until about 14:49:52Z. Because the Deployment has exactly 1 replica and no readiness/startup probe, the payment Service (selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment:8080) had no working backend during that gap: checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge recorded 81 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans while the payment server recorded only 1 error span, i.e. the calls failed before reaching a payment server. That failure propagated up the call path: checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder errors, frontend POST /api/checkout returning HTTP 500 (visible in frontend-proxy logs from 14:47:49.787Z to 14:49:52Z), frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' errors and finally frontend-proxy 'ingress' error spans (+80, from 500 to 580), which is the frontend-proxy request error rate the alert reports. frontend-proxy itself never restarted (same pod since 14:15:48Z, 0 restarts, Deployment generation 1), so the proxy is a propagation point, not the fault. A separate, pre-existing low-level 503 pattern (Envoy response flag UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on GET routes) exists before and after the burst and is a candidate for why a '>0' rule could fire at 14:47:31Z, 18s before the first observed 500; the exact rule expression could not be retrieved, so that timestamp detail is unverified.

claims.text: The payment Deployment in namespace otel-demo was rolled out at 14:47:44Z: ReplicaSet payment-79d86bf97f was created at 2026-11-16T14:47:44Z with 1 replica and its pod template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T14:47:44Z; the previous ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 (created 14:15:49Z) was scaled to 0 replicas. Its container spec is identical (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, same env, same cpu limit 20m / memory limit 160Mi), so this was a restart-style rollout, not an image or config change.

Deployment events for payment show the rollout sequence: ScalingReplicaSet payment 0->1 and SuccessfulCreate/Scheduled for pod payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t at 14:47:44Z, container Created 14:47:47Z and Started 14:47:48Z, then Killing 'Stopping container payment' for the old pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 and ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete at 14:47:49Z, and ScalingReplicaSet payment 1->0 at 14:47:49Z. No Evicted, OOMKilled or Failed event was returned.

The payment Deployment has replicas=1, strategy RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%, and its container declares no readinessProbe, no startupProbe and no livenessProbe. Service payment selects opentelemetry.io/name=payment on port 8080/targetPort 8080.

checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (STATUS_CODE_ERROR) had no series before the burst and then read 41 at 14:50:00Z, 80 at 14:51:00Z and 81 at 14:52:00Z and later; checkout's server span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder errored in exactly the same steps (41/80/81). In the same window payment's own server span grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge recorded only 1 STATUS_CODE_ERROR span (new instance) while its STATUS_CODE_UNSET counter ran to 356 by 15:00:00Z, i.e. the great majority of failed Charge calls produced no payment server error span.

Payment server spans stopped from the old pod and only resumed from the new pod inside the failure window: old exported_instance 03bc8207-f4b3-49bb-9e2f-be0ba778dff8 grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge STATUS_CODE_UNSET rose 612 (14:36:00Z) to 1079 (14:49:00Z) then stayed at 1079; new exported_instance f6e789fa-ff7e-4426-abbb-a2366174578f first appears at 14:52:00Z with 32 and reaches 356 at 15:00:00Z.

frontend-proxy logged POST /api/checkout as HTTP 500 (via_upstream, upstream frontend) from its first occurrence at container timestamp 2026-11-16T14:47:49.787Z through 14:49:52.401Z; 86 log lines with a 5xx status were present in the 14:45:00-14:56:00Z window, all of them on the frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-b9w85 pod.

frontend-proxy's own ingress error span counter jumped inside the same window: traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} read 495 at 14:36:00Z, 500 at 14:49:00Z, 543 at 14:50:00Z, 580 at 14:51:00Z, 583 at 14:52:00Z and 584-585 at 14:53:00-15:00:00Z (an increase of about 80 across the burst). frontend-proxy's 'router frontend egress' error spans existed only in the same burst.

The error burst was confined to roughly 14:45-14:55Z: 5-minute error increases for checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, frontend POST /api/checkout and frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' were 63.3/48/44.4 and then 0 from the 14:56:31Z evaluation onward, while frontend-proxy 'ingress' errors stayed non-zero at a low sporadic level (2.22 at 14:48:31Z, 1.19 at 14:56:31Z, 3.33 at 15:02:31Z, 3.53 at 15:04:31Z).

Only the payment workload changed in this window: every other otel-demo pod has startTime 2026-11-16T14:15:48-14:15:50Z with 0 restarts, and payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t is the only pod with startTime 14:47:44Z; frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-b9w85 started 14:15:48Z with 0 restarts and its Deployment is generation 1, while payment's Deployment is generation 2.

Before the incident the tracing data shows the same call path healthy: a sampled 14:15-14:30Z view of frontend/checkout/payment traces has error_rows 0 in every span group, with frontend-proxy ingress and 'router frontend egress' spans carrying http.status_code=200 and payment grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

The new payment pod's own logs show only successful processing ('Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.') from 14:53:49Z onward, with no error-level line, and its last termination is absent (no previous container instance, restartCount 0).

The 81 failed checkout Charge calls are the consequence of payment having no serving backend between the old pod's termination at 14:47:49Z and the new container beginning to serve at about 14:49:52Z (proxy 500s stop there), because the Deployment runs a single replica, the container has no readiness/startup probe so it was treated as available as soon as the container started (14:47:48Z), and the low cpu limit of 20m would slow application startup. Under this hypothesis the errors are connection-level (no payment server span) rather than application-level.

The alert's own start at 14:47:31Z precedes both the restart annotation (14:47:44Z) and the first logged checkout 500 (14:47:49.787Z). A pre-existing, low-volume 503 pattern on GET routes (Envoy response flag UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, seen at 14:35:18Z, 14:39:23Z, 14:39:55Z and 14:46:26Z) is a plausible separate trigger for a rule that fires on any error rate above 0; it is a much smaller contributor than the checkout burst and cannot be confirmed as the trigger because the rule definition was not retrievable.

Rejected: a new payment image or configuration change caused application errors. Both ReplicaSets use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment with identical env, resources and no probes; the only template difference is the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation on the new ReplicaSet.

Rejected: frontend-proxy itself was damaged or restarted. Pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-b9w85 started 2026-11-16T14:15:48Z with restartCount 0, container ready, Deployment frontend-proxy generation 1 with 1/1 available, and no Killing/OOM/Evicted event was returned for it; its error spans are downstream propagation of the frontend's 500s.

Rejected: payment returned application-level failures. payment's server-side Charge span recorded only 1 STATUS_CODE_ERROR span against 81 errored checkout client spans, and its logs show successful 'Transaction complete.' lines; the failures occurred before a payment server span existed.

Other backend services show no error increase attributable to this incident in the 25-minute error query: cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping, email, quote, accounting and image-provider error series are 0 or absent for their request operations; the only non-zero error series outside the checkout path are long-running flagd EventStream/Resolve client errors on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation plus flat baseline payment GET/dns.lookup/tcp.connect counters (1-2 each, unchanged over the window).

Give payment a readinessProbe (and preferably a startupProbe) on its gRPC port 8080 and either raise replicas above 1 or set rollingUpdate maxUnavailable to 0, so that a restart or rollout cannot remove the only serving payment backend while the replacement is still initializing at the current 20m CPU limit.

Review the RequestErrorRate rule for frontend-proxy: it is described as firing when the error rate is above 0 (reported current 0.0111111), which is sensitive to the sporadic 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} entries the proxy logs on GET routes even outside the incident; adding a small non-zero threshold or requiring sustained error rate would avoid alerting on single cancelled requests.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate rule expression, window and threshold could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no data for this Prometheus, so the reported value 0.01111111111111111 cannot be recomputed and the alert start at 14:47:31Z (13s before the restart annotation and 18s before the first logged checkout 500) cannot be attributed to a specific sample.

Jaeger contains no traces after about 2026-11-16T14:29:59Z (searches for checkout and frontend-proxy in 14:40-15:10Z returned no traces), so no span-level error detail (gRPC status, exception) is available for the failure window.
The frontend pod's logs could not be read (fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-f44st returned 0 lines), so the frontend's own exception text for the POST /api/checkout 500s is unknown.
The old payment pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 no longer exists and its container had no previous instance, so its final logs and termination details could not be inspected.

kube-state-metrics series (kube_pod_container_info, kube_deployment_status_*, kube_pod_owner) returned no data in this Prometheus, so pod-level resource metrics and image digests could not be checked; image identity was compared only through the ReplicaSet pod templates.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what issued the kubectl-style rollout restart of payment at 14:47:44Z is unknown.

Whether the alert is still firing after 14:53Z could not be established from the Alertmanager side; only the continuing low-level frontend-proxy ingress error spans (1.19-3.53 per 5 minutes) are visible in this Run.
next_steps: Inspect the RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition and its evaluation window outside this Run to confirm which sample produced the 14:47:31Z firing and to what degree the 1.1111% value reflects the 14:47:49-14:49:52Z checkout burst versus the sporadic 503s.
Use the change_history integration to identify the actor and method of the payment rollout restart at 2026-11-16T14:47:44Z.
Add a readiness/startup probe to the payment container and provide more than one replica or maxUnavailable=0, then re-test a rolling restart to confirm the charge-call gap disappears.

Consider raising the alert threshold above a single cancelled request, or excluding Envoy UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} 503s from the frontend-proxy error-rate calculation.
